articles.title: Mbappé: "¿El Balón de Oro? He hecho historia y es buen año, pero tienen que votar"
articles.standfirst: El delantero francés atendió a los medios en la rueda de prensa previa al debut en Champions ante el Inter
articles.summary: El delantero francés atendió a los medios en la rueda de prensa previa al debut en Champions ante el Inter
articles.body: Kylian Mbappé fue el elegido para atender a los medios en rueda de prensa en la previa del duelo ante el Inter. El francés afronta otra edición de Champions, la tercera vistiendo de blanco y la que seguramente quiera terminar conquistando por primera vez en su carrera. En su comparecencia habló sobre la posibilidad de ganar el Balón de Oro, las críticas sobre la implicación defensiva y la conexión con Vinicius. Partido de mañana y su estado: "Estamos muy felices de volver a jugar un partido de Champions. Jugamos con ilusión y determinación. El Bernabéu es una motivación más. Será exigente, pero es la Champions y es un placer enorme". Conexión con Vinicius: "No sé, es una opinión de millones. Es el club más grande y no puedo controlar qué se dice. Tenemos el mismo objetivo, que es ganar títulos. No podemos controlar la opinión de la gente. Intentamos siempre mejorar". Trabajo con Mou: "Tengo una visión más larga para la mejor versión de los once. Yo sé que a la gente le gusta hacer eso, es lo que vende, pero yo estoy en la mentalidad de pensar como equipo y mejorar". ¿Te sientes en deuda con el madridismo?: "Pienso únicamente en lo que viene. Pienso en cómo estar listo para el partido de mañana y ayudar al equipo". ¿Te mereces el Balón de Oro?: "Cuando juegas para el Madrid, la gente te asocia a este premio. Mucha gente me habla del Balón de Oro, es un tema positivo, he hecho historia este verano, pero vamos a ver. Es un buen año para eso y la gente tiene que votar". Implicación en defensa: "¿Solo yo y Vinicius? Tenemos que mejorar y es natural como jugador. Cada uno es diferente y tenemos que hacer las cosas de manera inteligente. No me gusta comparar. Es un debate sin fin. Todos tenemos que mejorar en este aspecto. Con balón también. Pero es la vida de un equipo de alto nivel". ¿Te sientes el mejor jugador del mundo?: "Yo siempre, pero es algo muy personal. Cada uno tiene su opinión. Unos pensarán que sí, otros que no. Es un debate... que no todos deben pensar como yo. Este año puede ser bueno para ganar el Balón de Oro, pero lo votan los periodistas y elegirán ellos". Dicen Mourinho ha vuelto para recuperar la vena competitiva. ¿Qué destacaría de él como entrenador?: "Es muy difícil responder a una pregunta que empieza con “se dice” ¿“Se dice” de quién? Es un tío que sabe ganar, contagiar alrededor. Y dar una motivación a todo el club, su grupo. Y ganar los partidos". ¿Ha habido una mejoría en el ambiente del vestuario respecto a la temporada pasada?: "Yo pienso que siempre ha habido buen ambiente y que debemos mejorar cosas, claro, como meter más goles. Pero estamos bien, tranquilos". Mourinho dijo que prefiere un Mbappé con 40 goles con títulos, que uno con 60 sin títulos. ¿Lo compra?: "Y compro menos, también. Incluso 30. No voy a decir que es un debate de gente que no juega al fútbol, pero sí uno absurdo. Si meto 40 y estamos peleando por Liga, Champions, Copa... ¿debo parar de meter goles porque si meto muchos? ¿No vamos a ganar? Claro que quiero ganar títulos, pero no es una cuestión de elegir. Debes hacer las dos. Marcar goles y ganar títulos". Derrota contra España en el Mundial y hambre por la Champions: "Son dos cosas distintas. Claro que no ganar el Mundial fue un momento difícil. Yo pienso que fue positivo para nosotros, para crear una conexión con el país y la energía. Hemos ganado uno, no podemos ganar siempre aunque queramos. Siempre tienes hambre de ganar después". Mejora en el aspecto táctico: "Tengo dos posiciones diferentes en la selección y aquí. Tengo que dar el paso adelante. Allí soy capitán y aquí no. Yo como jugador quiero mejorar, la percepción del juego, si atacamos o dominamos, la gestión de las emociones... He tenido varias visiones con varios entrenadores y eso me ha ayudado mucho. Hay muchos partidos en un partido". La relación entre las dos Champions ganadas por el PSG y su salida: "No lo puedo cambiar. No puedo hablar de manera general. Me da un poco igual. No sé todo del fútbol, pero sí más que mucha gente. Estoy tranquilo. A veces no son análisis, sino cosas que venden. Hablar de mí vende mucho".

articles.title: Champions League: Five key talking points for the 2026-27 season
articles.summary: Arsenal and Bayern lead the challengers to PSG, Mourinho aims for glory with Real and Italian minnows Como make debut.
articles.body:
This season’s league phase of the Champions League kicks off on Tuesday, with Real Madrid vs Inter Milan and Porto vs Man City among the standout games on the first evening.

Two-time defending champions Paris Saint-Germain are looking to make it three in a row and are the team to beat. In last week’s draw , they were handed meetings with Barcelona, Manchester City and Aston Villa, among their eight matches in the league phase of this season’s Champions League.

But several other teams fancy their chances of toppling the Parisians, including last year’s runners-up Arsenal, and Bayern Munich, who pushed PSG hard in the semifinal.

Meanwhile, Barcelona will expect to be among the favourites, while archrivals Real Madrid – now led for the second time by Jose Mourinho – will hope their Galacticos can power them to a final being held in their city, albeit at Atletico Madrid’s Metropolitano Stadium.

Here are the main talking points ahead of the new campaign.

PSG are the reigning back-to-back European champions after beating Arsenal in May’s final, and Luis Enrique now has the chance to become only the second coach to win three straight Champions Leagues with the same club, after Zinedine Zidane’s Real Madrid did it from 2016 to 18.

Indeed, only three clubs in the competition’s history have ever won three in a row – as well as Madrid, Ajax and Bayern Munich have also done it.

Perhaps sensibly, Enrique has decided to refine rather than rehaul his successful squad in preseason – adding Ferran Torres, Lucas Digne and Mika Godts while moving on Bradley Barcola, Goncalo Ramos and Lee Kang-in.

Harry Kane-powered Bayern make bid for greatness

Bayern go into the season chasing a third straight Bundesliga title under Vincent Kompany, having won last season by 16 points with a Bundesliga-record 122 goals. They are also desperate to go further in the Champions League, where they just fell short in a thrilling semifinal tie to PSG.

Harry Kane took the 2025-26 European Golden Shoe with 36 league goals in 31 appearances (61 in all competitions for Bayern, and another 12 for England), finishing well clear of rivals Erling Haaland and Kylian Mbappe.

At 33 and coming off a tough World Cup campaign, the question now is whether he can keep that pace up.

Bayern’s summer business has been more about retention than reinforcement – trying to fend off interest in Michael Olise and get him to extend his contract. Bayern probably just need some small tweaks around game management and the little bit of luck that every successful team needs to overhaul PSG this season.

Mourinho hopes for Madrid advantage in final

Madrid will be hoping to win the competition in their own city – if at a rival ground – with a squad expensively reinforced this summer by the likes of Bernardo Silva, Denzel Dumfries, Marc Cucurella and Yan Diomande.

They enjoyed a perfect start to their La Liga campaign by winning their first three games. But even during these victories, they still looked rusty and incoherent at times, and Mourinho’s side were handed a reality check on Friday as they were beaten 1-0 by Real Betis . The Portuguese veteran coach still has a lot of work to do to create a coherent team from its talented parts.

Como’s fairytale meets the Champions League

Como finished fourth in Serie A last season, qualifying for the Champions League for the first time in the club’s history. A club that was in Italy’s fourth tier a few years ago is now sharing a group stage with the continent’s biggest names under coach Cesc Fabregas.

The rise has been engineered by Indonesia’s Hartono family, who bought Como in 2019 and rebuilt them through three promotions in five years. They have kept investing into this summer too, with Real Madrid loanee Nico Paz signed permanently in June, a statement of intent that the last campaign was not a one-season fluke.

There are other minnows in the league stage – notably Norwegian champions Viking Stavanger and Azerbaijan’s Sabah FK – but perhaps none can match Como’s meteoric rise.

Villarreal and Real Betis show Spain’s strength in depth

Two Spanish clubs make their case for La Liga’s growing depth below Barcelona, Real Madrid, and Atletico Madrid. Villarreal finished third last season to qualify directly for the Champions League for the first time in more than a decade.

Manuel Pellegrini’s Real Betis – playing in their first Champions League campaign since 2005-06 – reached the competition via Spain’s newly expanded fifth spot, earned after Rayo Vallecano’s run to the Conference League final.

Neither Villarreal nor Betis has the financial muscle of the continent’s heavyweights, but both arrive with momentum and points to prove.

articles.title: Grupos externos al Madrid promueven acciones en apoyo a Ceuta ante el Inter
articles.standfirst: Diversos movimientos en Redes Sociales critican la inacción del club y piden a la afición acudir al Bernabéu con banderas ceutíes
articles.summary: Diversos movimientos en Redes Sociales critican la inacción del club y piden a la afición acudir al Bernabéu con banderas ceutíes
articles.body: El madridismo se está movilizando para mostrar su apoyo a Ceuta en el partido de Champions de este martes frente al Inter. Las Redes Sociales están sirviendo de herramienta aglutinadora para unir a los aficionados blancos en la expresión de apoyo a Ceuta, que desde hace semanas vive una situación que ha causado enorme alarma social. Estos grupos externos al Madrid, sin aparente conexión entre sí, han mostrado su malestar con la entidad madridista por no haber mostrado ya su apoyo a dicha ciudad en un momento tan delicado. Hasta el punto de que algunos medios llegaron a vincular (sin ningún tipo de prueba) esta inacción del club a una prohibición expresa de Anas Laghrari, el empresario marroquí que actúa en la sombra como mano derecha de Florentino Pérez. Este asunto es difícilmente creíble, pero ha servido para agitar aún más el movimiento popular. Algunos periodistas de mucho predicamento entre el madridismo también están impulsando esta campaña de apoyo a Ceuta aprovechando el partido de Champions ante el Inter de Milán. El club, de momento, no se ha pronunciado en torno a si dejará pasar al estadio banderas ceutíes o incluso si, activado por el clamor popular, organizará en último instante alguna acción de carácter oficial. Por todos es sabido que la visibilidad que aporta el Madrid a cualquier asunto es gigantesca. El fútbol, y la Champions, es un altavoz formidable. De hecho, los aficionados marroquíes también aprovecharon un partido de fútbol para lanzar sus sorprendentes e inaceptables mensajes. El fútbol africano vivió este fin de semana un episodio que trascendió por completo lo deportivo: los aficionados del Maghreb Association Sportive de Fez (MAS Fez, el campeón de Marruecos) desplegaron una enorme pancarta en las gradas del Complexe Sportif de Fez con el mensaje "Ceuta y Melilla: dos ciudades, una patria: Marruecos", aprovechando el estreno de su equipo en la Liga de Campeones de la CAF frente al Rahimo FC de Burkina Faso. La acción se produjo en uno de los fondos del estadio y fue protagonizada por seguidores vinculados al grupo ultra Fatal Tigers, uno de los colectivos más numerosos de la afición del club marroquí. El tifo, redactado íntegramente en español, permaneció visible durante los primeros minutos del encuentro y fue acompañado por cánticos y un importante despliegue de banderas en la grada. El episodio llega, además, en un momento especialmente sensible para las relaciones futbolísticas entre ambos países, con España, Portugal y Marruecos ya inmersos en la organización conjunta del Mundial 2030, un proyecto que exige una colaboración estrecha entre las tres federaciones justo cuando este tipo de gestos vuelven a poner sobre la mesa las diferencias territoriales de fondo. En Cornellà, otro futbolista quiso sumar su propio gesto de apoyo a Ceuta. Marcos Fernández tardó hasta el minuto 98 en estrenar su casillero goleador en Primera División, y el tanto llegó cargado de significado: el delantero del Espanyol firmó el 1-1 definitivo ante el Sevilla y, tras el pitido del gol, se subió la camiseta para mostrar una pancarta interior con la frase "Ceuta no se vende, Ceuta se defiende". El vínculo del jugador con la ciudad autónoma viene de la temporada pasada, cuando militó cedido en la AD Ceuta. Ya en zona mixta, Marcos explicó el porqué del gesto: quiso emplear su primer gol en la máxima categoría para dedicárselo a una ciudad que, según sus palabras, "me acogió espectacular, como si fuese uno más de ellos". El delantero cerró sus declaraciones enviando "toda la fuerza del mundo" a los ceutíes y deseando que la situación que atraviesa la ciudad "se solucione lo antes posible".

articles.title: Manchester City’s blockbuster summer signing wanted Real Madrid ‘at all costs’ but club said no
articles.summary: Enzo Fernandez reportedly saw Real Madrid as a potential escape route from Chelsea before Manchester City eventually emerged as his destination this summer.A...
articles.body:
Enzo Fernandez reportedly saw Real Madrid as a potential escape route from Chelsea before Manchester City eventually emerged as his destination this summer.

According to AS , the Argentine midfielder was determined to leave Stamford Bridge and believed there could be an opening for him at the Spanish giants.

Fernandez even made his interest known and flirted with the possibility of moving to the Santiago Bernabeu 'at all costs'.

Real Madrid, however, did not share the same enthusiasm.

In fact, it is important to remember that the Spanish club publicly denied interest in the midfielder, closing off the route Fernandez had hoped would lead him away from Chelsea.

That rejection ultimately helped influence the transfer picture.

Enzo Fernandez wanted Real Madrid move 'at all costs'. (Photo by Naomi Baker/Getty Images)

With Real Madrid out of the equation, Manchester City were able to take advantage of the situation and complete a blockbuster deal for the former Benfica and River Plate player.

Fernandez's desire to leave Chelsea was clear from the early stages of the transfer window.

He believed Real Madrid represented a realistic opportunity, but the Spanish club's response made it clear that there was no reciprocal interest.

The situation left Fernandez with fewer options, and the Premier League became the most realistic destination.

Manchester City were waiting in the background and eventually moved decisively to secure his signature.

Enzo Fernandez ultimately signed for Manchester City. (Photo by Naomi Baker/Getty Images)

The report suggests the midfielder's flirtation with Madrid ultimately proved a mistake, as the club's refusal to engage narrowed his choices considerably.

Manchester City turn rejection into opportunity

Manchester City capitalised on the circumstances to land Fernandez for €145 million, a fee that could eventually rise further with additional payments.

The transfer has also pushed Fernandez into elite territory when it comes to the money generated by his career moves.

His three transfers have now produced a combined €310 million, placing him third in the all-time ranking of players who have generated the most transfer income.

Only Neymar and Romelu Lukaku sit above him. Neymar has generated €400 million across three transfers, while Lukaku has reached €375 million through ten separate deals.

articles.title: Barcelona defender already back in training and will play against Levante after nose injury
articles.summary: Barcelona have received positive news on Eric Garcia after the versatile defender suffered another nose injury during Sunday’s emphatic victory over Valencia...
articles.body:
Barcelona have received positive news on Eric Garcia after the versatile defender suffered another nose injury during Sunday's emphatic victory over Valencia.

According to a report from SPORT , Garcia has suffered a nasal fracture but is not expected to miss Barcelona's next La Liga fixture against Levante.

The versatile defender, who is now one of Barcelona's captains , has already returned to training wearing a protective mask and is targeting a return next Sunday.

It is to be noted that Garcia was forced off in the 29th minute at Mestalla after an accidental collision with Rodri.

The pair challenged for a corner, and Rodri's head struck Garcia's already vulnerable nose, leaving the defender visibly upset as he made his way off the pitch.

Eric Garcia injured his nose against Valencia. (Photo by David Ramos/Getty Images)

Despite the initial concern surrounding the injury, Barcelona are now optimistic that Garcia can feature against Levante.

Garcia already training with protective mask

The latest update will come as a relief to Hansi Flick, who has relied heavily on Garcia at right-back during the opening weeks of the season.

The defender has started three of Barcelona's first four league matches, with Flick preferring him to Jules Kounde in the position.

Hence, his return to training on Monday is particularly encouraging. He worked at the Ciutat Esportiva while wearing a mask designed to protect his nose from further damage.

The precaution is familiar territory for the Barcelona academy product, as Garcia already suffered a fractured nasal septum last season and spent almost two months wearing a protective mask after that injury.

This time, however, Barcelona do not expect the fracture to keep him out for an extended period.

Champions League suspension delays Garcia's return

Garcia's immediate absence will instead come in Europe rather than because of his latest injury.

The defender will miss Barcelona's Champions League opener against Feyenoord at the Spotify Camp Nou after being sent off in the second leg of last season's quarter-final against Atletico Madrid.

That suspension means Garcia will be unavailable for the European fixture regardless of his physical condition, giving him additional time to recover before Barcelona's trip to face Levante.

articles.title: Trinidad Chambliss Takes Blame for 'Bad Decisions' and Hypes Ole Miss WR Deuce Alexander
articles.summary: No. 9 Ole Miss escaped with a 41-38 win over No. 24 Louisville in Sunday's season opener, but quarterback Trinidad Chambliss wasn't pleased with his performance in the victory.
articles.body:
No. 9 Ole Miss escaped with a 41-38 win over No. 24 Louisville in Sunday's season opener, but quarterback Trinidad Chambliss wasn't pleased with his performance in the victory.

It was clear that the Rebels were in for a long night when the ball was snapped over Chambliss' head on the second play from scrimmage. The senior signal-caller also lost a fumble and threw an interception in the first half before Ole Miss needed a last-second 48-yard field goal from Lucas Carneiro to earn the three-point win.

"You obviously don't want to start like that," Chambliss said after the game, per ESPN's Mark Schlabach . "I'm making bad decisions, turning over the ball, not being comfortable in the pocket, and just not playing the type of ball I'm capable of. I guess I had to just get used to playing again."

Watch: Punt of the year contender in CFB

Besides the two turnovers, Chambliss had a solid outing, completing 21 of his 36 passes for 336 yards and three touchdowns. He also registered nine carries for 60 yards and another score.

However, the star of the show was junior wide receiver Deuce Alexander, who caught a pair of 62-yard touchdowns from Chambliss and finished with five catches for 159 yards. Schlabach noted that Ole Miss head coach Pete Golding previously worked at Alabama as a defensive coordinator and "compared Alexander to former Crimson Tide star wide receiver Jameson Williams because of Alexander's elite speed." His quarterback had high praise for him as well.

"He's just a playmaker," Chambliss said of Alexander. "We knew that going into the year. He's one of the best receivers in the country, and we've got to use him."

Ole Miss will hope for a more dominant performance when it hosts Charlotte in its home opener in Week 2. The Rebels will need all the momentum they can get before a highly anticipated showdown against LSU and former head coach Lane Kiffin on Sept. 19.

articles.title: Women's Super League: Alexia Putellas' debut for London City analysed with more on Man City and Chelsea
articles.summary: Digital journalist Laura Hunter returns for a second season with a WSL-dedicated column, analysing all the big talking points from across the weekend's action; London City Lionesses' winning start is this week's big focus, with more on Manchester City and Chelsea
articles.body:
Putellas only part of London City's style meets substance - will it last?

Michele Kang rolled out the red carpet in Bromley for London City Lionesses' season opener under the lights, where the Sky Sports cameras were in attendance to watch a dominant win over Manchester United. Kang herself was among the spectators in a sell-out crowd.

Alexia Putellas inevitably made all the headlines. The two-time Ballon d'Or winner commands that kind of attention. But the real standouts from such a positive opening night, in footballing terms, were Delphine Cascarino and Danielle van de Donk. Neither part of this summer's spending spree but the two most influential players on the park.

London City gave a good account of themselves in most departments, actually. A performance far more complete than the majority of last season, or even the sum of all their individual parts suggested.

Putellas was sound, if not as spectacular. It will take time for her to acclimatise to new surroundings, or perhaps more appropriately, take patience for those surroundings to adapt to her. It has always been that way around for La Reina. Team-mates must reach her wavelength.

What was clear is that the Spain superstar will be the nucleus of Eder Maestre's plan. Of the eight chances London City created, she claimed two and Cascarino was responsible for four. The restless Putellas hype will no doubt carry through the season, her standards acting as the spine and soul of this group of newcomers. She has to knit all the various pieces together to meet the required level of chemistry that constitute a team.

But Maestre's side look to have gelled fairly well on first glance. No doubt they will face sterner tests in future weeks. London City and Man Utd were actually the perfect antithesis for opening night, a side on their way up passing one in obvious decline. London City barely stopped to say hello.

Kang's empire has consumed Bromley and will continue to dominate WSL chatter for as long as their results match their endeavour. There is no denying the pull of Putellas. Or Cascarino. Or Mary Earps, who did not feature on Friday but was still a major fan attraction. But buying footballers is really the easy part. Creating a consistent team out of them much more difficult.

It's only week one and Khadija 'Bunny' Shaw has reaffirmed her position as the best the Women's Super League has to offer, her 11 shots yielding two goals as Man City beat Birmingham.

Nothing about that victory was especially experimental, though still impressive. Shaw scored two carbon-copy goals, both from corners, both delivered from the left. Her movement for each was similar except the angle of the second header was far more difficult to guide on target. She made it look easy.

City scored 15 times from corners last season, a seasonal record, and such a superpower will no doubt come in handy again as they look to defend their crown. They were the only side to score from a set-piece across opening weekend. Last term, they scored from a set-play in all but seven games.

But what struck me was how lop-sided their attacking phase was from open play. Almost everything went through Lauren Hemp. Loading on the left is not necessarily a new tactic, but to such an extent surely misses an opportunity.

Hemp is an exceptional outlet, with pace to burn and superb crossing accuracy, which is why the centre-backs often look left when playing out from the back. Gracie Prior found Hemp 11 times against Birmingham. Opponents know to expect this.

Where City might profit this term is by exploiting that expectancy to unlock different pockets of space. Use the threat of Hemp to attract numbers and play elsewhere. Andree Jeglertz has spoken plenty about wanting City to have fresh, innovative ways of creating goals. He likes central rotations, utilising the ball-playing skill of Yui Hasegawa. City should lean into her passing range more.

Perhaps that will be helped by Vivianne Miedema's return from injury, whenever that might be. But before then, they can also afford to mix it up a bit more. Becoming even more versatile than they are now could propel them from being a very good team to an unbeatable one.

New season, same problem for Chelsea. Their creators are crying out for a finisher.

Lauren James cannot be expected to shoulder the scoring burden on her own. So, how can Chelsea combat a flaw that has been plaguing them since Sonia Bompastor took charge?

Stylistically, Chelsea are doing most things right. A statistical reading of their 1-1 draw with Aston Villa will tell you that final-third entries were plentiful. The Blues created five big chances, missing four.

Essentially, James has been left to do the job of a winger and striker. She created the joint-most chances for others (4) while taking the most shots herself (11). Aggie Beever-Jones accumulated the highest expected goals total but debutant goalkeeper Akane Okuma was equal to both of her two efforts on target, neither particularly taxing.

The speed at which Chelsea arrive in the box remains an issue. It allows enough retreating defenders to make blocks; Villa made six of them. Okuma also made a remarkable nine saves. "We have to speed up the game," reflected Bompastor.

Chelsea's 35 shots were their most ever in a league game they failed to win. Bompastor added: "If you analyse the statistics, you would say it's crazy that we didn't win." The club's succession line of attackers looks too thin given what they are up against. They have Melvine Malard and Mayra Ramirez to return. But they need firepower now.
